title: Rubrics as an Attack Surface: Stealthy Preference Drift in LLM Judges

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring systematic directional shifts (preference drift) in LLM judge evaluations on helpfulness target domains (e.g., Ultra-Real, Ultra-Creative) by comparing the judge's preference labels under modified, benchmark-compliant rubrics against human reference labels, and evaluating the resulting downstream policy using reward models and pairwise win-rates.

Measuring directional degradation in safety judgments (e.g., systematic over-refusal for benign queries) on harmlessness target domains (e.g., Anthropic-SafeRLHF) by applying adversarial safety rubrics to LLM judges and evaluating the impact on policies trained on these biased labels.
